answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a nontransferable stake in a vault before it can submit work, then slash that stake when independent reviewers confirm fraud or duplicate control. New identities also face a capped earning rate until they build a record, so splitting one actor across many accounts does not multiply immediate influence. A legitimate entrant pays an opportunity cost; a sybil attacker must lock more copper and risk losing it, while waiting for each umber-marked account to earn trust.
